$comment: Declarative gate registry for the golden-path corpus. Adding a gate is an entry here,
not a new script. Run `node scripts/census/run-census.mjs --help` for the contract.
id           stable slug; also the --rule filter value
goldenPath   the doc that owns this rule. A rule with no owner is a rule nobody maintains.
pattern is matched against WHOLE FILE CONTENT, never line-by-line
exclude      [{ path, reason }] — reason is REQUIRED and enforced (>= 12 chars).
An exclude that matches no file fails the run (stale exemption).
baseline     { files, matches } — the run fails if either RISES, and also if either
DROPS without this being updated (a silent drop is usually a broken matcher)
floor        minimum files the walk must SEE. Below it, the result is untrustworthy
and the run fails with 'matcher broken, not codebase clean'.

rules.title: Code-split boundary declared with raw React.lazy instead of lazyRetry

signal.description: a chunk boundary declared with raw React.lazy(); lazyRetry() is the drop-in that survives a failed chunk fetch instead of caching the rejection forever (2026-06-07 incident). Proxy for: a dynamic-import boundary with no recovery path.

rules.title: Feature-local empty-state component instead of ScenarioEmptyState

signal.description: a component declared in a feature folder to render a settled-empty region. Proxy for: this surface answers "what do I show when there is nothing" by authoring a new component rather than selecting a condition on the shared one — so no condition taxonomy (first-use / filtered-to-zero / prerequisite-not-met / errored) can reach it. The extracted-and-named shape is a house accident, NOT the condition: personas-web has the same condition at the same scale and this pattern scores ~0 there, because its hand-rolls stay inline.

rules.title: Deferred transaction whose first statement is a SELECT that informs a later write

signal.description: a DEFERRED transaction (BEGIN, not BEGIN IMMEDIATE) whose first use of `tx` is a literal SELECT and which later writes through the same `tx` — the SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT shape

exclude.reason: migrations run inside init_db_with_journal (db/src/lib.rs:332-333) before any other consumer holds a pooled connection, so there is no concurrent writer to lose the snapshot to; the boot-migration-step golden path owns this phase

rules.title: Row-set read that discards per-row mapping failures without logging

signal.description: a rusqlite query_map row iterator reduced by filter_map(|r| r.ok()) / filter_map(Result::ok) / .flatten() — the row and the evidence both disappear and the caller still gets Ok. Anchored to query_map because all three are generic Rust idioms; unanchored, .flatten() alone matches hundreds of Option chains. PROXY FOR the stack-free condition "a row-set read discards a per-row mapping failure without recording it" — an adopting repo must re-derive its own proxy (see the golden path §9). PRECONDITION: this repo reduces row iterators with iterator adapters within ~700 chars of the query_map( call and does not wrap them in helpers. 8/8 sampled matches were true positives; 4 of the 148 sit in #[cfg(test)] modules and are carried in the baseline rather than excluded, because excluding them means excluding three whole production files. The two legal policies are `collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()` (propagate) and `collect_rows(rows, "table::op")` (skip AND log).
